proposals.before: When Emperor Yuan prepared to cross south of the Yangzi, Wang Kuang had been the first to advance the plan.
proposals.after: When Emperor Yuan crossed south of the Yangzi, Wang Kuang had been the first to advance the plan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 過江也 narrates the crossing as an accomplished event, not a preparation still in prospect.

proposals.before: For years the remnant population has been bled white; shackled convicts choke the highways—policy almost as harsh as the Qin, short only of mass executions by kinship. I fear a Chen Sheng–style uprising may not be far off.
proposals.after: For years the remnant population has been bled white; shackled convicts choke the highways—policy almost as harsh as the Qin, short only of mass executions by kinship. I fear the worry of Chen Sheng and Wu Guang may not be far off.
proposals.reason: Chinese 勝廣 names both Chen Sheng and Wu Guang; the idiomatic rendering drops Wu Guang.

proposals.before: Hopefully slowly seek the hearts of the multitude.
proposals.after: I hope you will gradually seek the confidence of the multitude.
proposals.reason: Literal English is ungrammatical and obscures 幸徐求眾心 as a courteous hortative.

proposals.before: The gone cannot be remonstrated; the coming still can be pursued; I wish the Prince again drop three thoughts, untie and restring, causing Yin Hao, Xun Xian to return and occupy Hefei, Guangling, Xuchang, Qiao commandery, Liang, Pengcheng various armies all return to guard the Huai, as foundation of invincibility; when beard root stands momentum rises, planning it is not late—this truly is of present strategies the highest.
proposals.after: The gone cannot be remonstrated; the coming still can be pursued; I wish the Prince again drop three thoughts, untie and restring, causing Yin Hao, Xun Xian to return and occupy Hefei, Guangling, Xuchang, Qiao commandery, Liang, Pengcheng various armies all return to guard the Huai, as foundation of invincibility; when the roots stand and momentum rises, planning it is not late—this truly is of present strategies the highest.
proposals.reason: 鬚根立勢舉 is a graphic error or forced reading of 須根立勢舉; 'beard root' is not the military-logistical metaphor.

proposals.before: In normal times south of the Yangzi a single capable Inspector of Yang province was enough to keep order; with so many talented men under you, disorder persists only because regulations conflict and too many hands pull in different directions. Simplify the rules so they are easy to obey, and you can preserve what we have
proposals.after: In normal times south of the Yangzi a single capable Inspector of Yang province was enough to keep order; with so many talented men under you, disorder persists only because regulations conflict and too many hands pull in different directions. Simplify the rules so they are easy to obey, and that will suffice to preserve the enterprise already achieved.
proposals.reason: The English sentence is truncated and leaves 便足以保守成業 unfinished.

proposals.before: Solidly knowing equating death and life is empty absurdity, equalizing Peng and shang is reckless making; later's viewing now, also like now's viewing past—alas!
proposals.after: Solidly knowing that equating death and life is empty absurdity, and that equalizing Peng Zu with a child dead young is reckless invention; later ages viewing the present are also like the present viewing the past—alas!
proposals.reason: Literal leaves 殤 untranslated as 'shang' and does not identify 彭 as Peng Zu, obscuring the longevity contrast.

proposals.before: General-in-Chief Who Inspires Awe Wang Shu had enjoyed some fame and was ranked with Wang Xizhi, but Xizhi despised him, and the two never got along.
proposals.after: General of Agile Cavalry Wang Shu had enjoyed some fame and was ranked with Wang Xizhi, but Xizhi despised him, and the two never got along.
proposals.reason: 驃騎將軍 is the Agile Cavalry generalship, not a title meaning who inspires awe.

proposals.before: Liu Dan was governor of Danyang. Xu Xun once stayed the night: fresh curtains, rich food.
proposals.after: Liu Tan was governor of Danyang. Xu Xun once stayed the night: fresh curtains, rich food.
proposals.reason: 惔 is Tan, not Dan; the established romanization of 劉惔 is Liu Tan.

proposals.before: At the time Liu Dan was Danyang Governor; Xu Xun once went to Dan to lodge, bed curtains new and lovely, drink and food abundant sweet.
proposals.after: At the time Liu Tan was Danyang Governor; Xu Xun once went to Tan to lodge, bed curtains new and lovely, drink and food abundant sweet.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 惔 as Dan, and 'Dan' as the lodging host's name.

proposals.before: He died at fifty-nine and was posthumously honored as Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
proposals.after: Wang Xizhi died at fifty-nine and was posthumously honored as Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
proposals.reason: The silent subject of 年五十九卒 is Wang Xizhi, continued by his sons' refusal and the 子凝之 heading; the preceding sentence is about Xie Wan's defeat and the English 'He' wrongly attaches the death to Xie Wan.

proposals.before: His sons, obeying his earlier wishes, firmly declined the enfeoffment.
proposals.after: His sons, obeying his earlier wishes, firmly declined the posthumous honor.
proposals.reason: 固讓不受 continues 贈金紫光祿大夫, a posthumous honor, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: He later served as cavalry adviser to Huan Chong, the Cavalry-in-Attendant. Huan Chong asked, "Which section are you attached to?"
proposals.after: He later served as cavalry adviser to Huan Chong, the General of Chariot and Cavalry. Huan Chong asked, "Which section are you attached to?"
proposals.reason: 車騎 here is the general's title 車騎將軍, not Cavalry-in-Attendant.

proposals.before: He later served as a Palace Attendant, then quit and went east. He and Xianzhi both lay near death when a occultist said, "When a man's span is up, if another willingly trades his years, the dying man may live."
proposals.after: He later served as a Palace Attendant, then quit and went east. He and Xianzhi both lay near death when an occultist said, "When a man's span is up, if another willingly trades his years, the dying man may live."
proposals.reason: Unnatural English: the article before occultist must be an, not a.

proposals.before: His son: Wang Caozhi
proposals.after: Wang Caozhi
proposals.reason: Heading 子 操之 continues Wang Xizhi's sons after Huizhi's cadet line; Caozhi is Xianzhi's elder brother in s0258, not Zhenzhi's son.

proposals.before: His son: Wang Xianzhi
proposals.after: Wang Xianzhi
proposals.reason: Heading 子 獻之 is Wang Xizhi's son, not Caozhi's child; s0258 names Huizhi and Caozhi as Xianzhi's elder brothers.

proposals.before: When Empress Anxi was installed, her father Wang Xianzhi was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, Specially Advanced, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Grand Governor with the posthumous title "Xian."
proposals.after: When Empress Anxi was installed, her father Wang Xianzhi was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, Specially Advanced, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Grand Steward, with the posthumous title "Xian."
proposals.reason: 太宰 is Grand Steward, not Grand Governor; the idiomatic office name is wrong.

proposals.before: Your Majesty ascended the throne; yang-autumn still plentiful, exhausting heart and exhausting wisdom to assist sagely brightness.
proposals.after: Your Majesty ascended the throne; his years were still plentiful, exhausting heart and exhausting wisdom to assist sagely brightness.
proposals.reason: 陽秋 is a taboo-avoiding term for years/age (春秋), not the calque yang-autumn, which obscures that Xie An was still in his prime.

proposals.before: The historian's judgment runs: Writing arose in high antiquity from knotted cords and bird-track glyphs—scarcely worth our notice.
proposals.after: The historian's judgment runs: The rise of writing began in middle antiquity; knotted-cord patterns and bird-track glyphs are scarcely worth our notice.
proposals.reason: 中古 is middle antiquity, not high antiquity, and 繩文鳥跡 are dismissed as unworthy predecessors rather than identified as the origin of writing.

proposals.before: Only from Zhong Yao and the Wangs onward can one speak with confidence.
proposals.after: Only from Zhong Yao and Wang onward can one speak with confidence.
proposals.reason: 鐘王 is the conventional pair Zhong Yao and Wang (Xizhi), a singular Wang, not a plural Wang clan.

proposals.before: Combining these two, therefore brush-ink's sickness sucks!
proposals.after: Combining these two, therefore it is a sickness of brush and ink!
proposals.reason: 歙 here is a rhetorical or exclamatory close, commonly 歟, not the English verb sucks.

decisions.reason: The clause 元帝之過江也 sets the crossing as a narrated event; 過江 is not a still-pending preparation. The pluperfect in the replacement still allows Kuang's proposal to precede the crossing.

decisions.after: For years the remnant population has been bled white; shackled convicts choke the highways—policy almost as harsh as the Qin, short only of mass executions by kinship. I fear a Chen Sheng and Wu Guang–style uprising may not be far off.
decisions.reason: 勝廣 names both rebels; omitting Wu Guang is a real error. The proposed 'worry of Chen Sheng and Wu Guang' calques 勝廣之憂 as anxiety belonging to those men, whereas the phrase warns of a Sheng–Guang style revolt, as 無復日矣 already implies it is near.
幸徐求眾心 is a courteous hortative, not a fragmentary 'Hopefully slowly seek…'. The replacement restores grammar and the addressee of Yin Hao's letter.

CText and other editions read 須根立勢舉, a wait-until-the-roots-stand metaphor after 為不可勝之基. The chapter's 鬚 yields the false calque 'beard root'; the replacement matches the intended military sense without rewriting the rest of the literal sentence.
The inherited English stops short of 便足以保守成業. 便足以 is 'then it will suffice,' and 成業 is the enterprise already achieved, not a dangling 'what we have'.
齊彭殤 contrasts Peng Zu with 殤, a child dead young; leaving 殤 as 'shang' and 彭 as bare 'Peng' hides that contrast, and 'reckless making' is not English for 妄作.
驃騎將軍 is the Agile Cavalry generalship. 'General-in-Chief Who Inspires Awe' invents a semantic title the Chinese does not carry.
劉惔 is Liu Tan; 惔 is not Dan. The surrounding 就惔宿 and 惔曰 name the same man.
The same 惔 is the host of 就惔宿; rendering him twice as Dan is a naming error in the literal field.
After 萬不能用，果敗, English 'He died' would attach to Xie Wan. 年五十九卒 and the following 諸子…子凝之 resume Wang Xizhi's biography.
固讓不受 continues 贈金紫光祿大夫, a posthumous honor, not an enfeoffment.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 諸子遵父先旨，固讓不受

decisions.reason: 車騎桓沖 is Huan Chong titled by the Chariot-and-Cavalry generalship (車騎將軍), distinct from the 騎兵參軍 post Huizhi held. Cavalry-in-Attendant is the wrong office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又為車騎桓沖騎兵參軍

decisions.reason: 'A occultist' is ungrammatical English before a vowel-initial noun; the Chinese 術人 is unchanged.
The heading 子操之 resumes Wang Xizhi's sons after Huizhi's cadet line (楨之). 'His son' after Zhenzhi's speech would make Caozhi Zhenzhi's child, which 子操之 does not say.
子獻之 is the next brother-heading under Xizhi, not Caozhi's son; treating Xianzhi as Caozhi's child is a kinship error.
太宰 is Grand Steward. Grand Governor is a wrong office name for the posthumous grant listed after 光祿大夫.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 追贈侍中、特進、光祿大夫、太宰

decisions.reason: 陽秋尚富 is the Jin taboo writing of 春秋尚富, 'years still plentiful,' of Xie An who then 盡心竭智以輔聖明. The calque 'yang-autumn' hides that age/prime sense.
肇乎中古 is middle antiquity, not high antiquity. 繩文鳥跡，不足可觀 is a separate dismissal of knotted-cord and bird-track graphs, not the origin identified with 書契之興.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 書契之興，肇乎中古，繩文鳥跡，不足可觀

decisions.reason: 鐘王 is the pair Zhong and Wang (Xizhi), continued by 鐘雖擅美一時. Plural 'the Wangs' invents a clan where the text names one Wang.
CText reads 故翰墨之病歟, a rhetorical close. Translating chapter 歙 as the English verb 'sucks' is a false reading; the sentence names the two faults as a sickness of brush and ink.

claimRevisions.reason: The extracted English title was produced by the false rendering of 驃騎將軍; the office is General of Agile Cavalry.
The office label repeats the invented 'Who Inspires Awe' title; 驃騎將軍 is unchanged in Chinese.
The English personal name Liu Dan was created by misreading 惔; the man is Liu Tan, already indicated by the stored pinyin.
The given-name English Dan contradicts 惔 / Tan; the repair restores the given name without dropping the attestation.
